title: Private min pack: add Runtime Performance dashboard (prefill vs decode, queue depth, batching, KV cache) + cardinality notes
author: Sergio Costa
description:
Adds the initial "Runtime Performance" Grafana dashboard for the Private Observability Minimum Pack. The goal is day-1 visibility into runtime bottlenecks and saturation with a consistent latency breakdown (prefill vs decode), queueing, batching behavior, and KV cache effectiveness. Panels are built to work in both VPC and on-prem Private installs and follow the standard templating introduced in #318 and the folder/naming conventions from #319.

Dashboard: "Private / Runtime Performance" (folder: "Private Min Pack")
- Latency breakdown: prefill vs decode (p50/p95/p99) with request-rate overlay
- Queue depth and time-in-queue: shows scheduler/engine backlog and correlates with tail latency
- Batch behavior: batch size distribution, continuous batching efficiency, tokens/s vs requests/s
- KV cache: hit rate (prefix/KV), cache evictions, and cache memory pressure proxy
- "At a glance" health row: 5xx rate + runtime restarts + throttling indicators (where available)

Templating/variables
- $cluster, $namespace (required)
- $component (runtime deployment label selector)
- $tenant (optional; hidden by default)
- $model (optional; hidden by default)

Cardinality constraints (added as annotations + README notes)
- Dashboard queries prefer aggregations that drop high-cardinality labels. The panel queries intentionally do not group by request_id, prompt_hash, or per-worker IDs.
- $tenant and $model variables are optional and default to "All"; panels fall back to cluster-level aggregations. Guidance is included for operators on when to enable tenant/model drilldowns.
- PromQL examples use sum/avg over (cluster, namespace, route, model) only where needed; otherwise aggregation is at (cluster, namespace).

Notes / dependencies
- This PR assumes metric names/labels defined in the Private minimum signals draft (in-progress); where metrics are not yet emitted, panels are present but include "no data" helper text and a link to the metrics contract issue (ENG-2845).

Follow-ups (out of scope here)
- Add runtime per-GPU breakdown once the GPU label strategy is finalized (avoid per-device explosion).
- Add queueing heatmap once histogram buckets are stabilized across runtime versions.

Screenshots
- Attached in PR discussion: runtime dashboard with prefill/decode row + queue/batch/cache rows (staging env).

illustrative_snippets: Panel query (prefill p95): histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, cluster, namespace) (rate(redwood_runtime_prefill_latency_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", component=~"$component"}[5m])))

Panel query (decode p95): histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, cluster, namespace) (rate(redwood_runtime_decode_latency_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", component=~"$component"}[5m])))
Panel query (queue depth): max by (cluster, namespace) (redwood_runtime_scheduler_queue_depth{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", component=~"$component"})

Cardinality note (dashboard text panel): "Avoid enabling tenant+model breakdown on busy clusters unless you have validated label cardinality. Redwood support baseline assumes cluster/namespace aggregation."
review_conversation:
Allison Grant: Can we be explicit in the dashboard itself about which labels are safe to group by? We keep seeing customers accidentally turning on per-worker breakdowns and Prometheus falls over. Sergio Costa: Added a "Cardinality & label guidance" collapsible row at the top + inline notes in each query using a consistent pattern (drop request_id/worker_id). Also defaulted tenant/model variables to hidden.

Omar El-Sayed: Prefill vs decode units look inconsistent across panels. Are these all seconds? Sergio Costa: Yes; cleaned up panel units to "s" everywhere and added a tooltip clarifying prefill=prompt processing, decode=token generation. Also switched a couple of panels from avg to histogram_quantile to avoid misleading results.

Julian Moore: Queue depth panel uses max(). For multi-scheduler replicas, max might hide imbalances. Consider sum + add a "topk" panel? Sergio Costa: Agree. Updated to show both: (1) sum(queue_depth) for total backlog and (2) topk(5, queue_depth) in a small table for skew without exploding series.

Logan Wright: KV cache hit rate formula? We should make sure this doesn't imply a strict correctness guarantee. Sergio Costa: Added help text: hit rate is a best-effort proxy based on cache hit counters; not a quality signal. Also added a panel for eviction count rate so operators can correlate drops in hit rate.

Allison Grant (final): Thanks. The inline guidance is what we need for "supported". Approving once CI is green.
